newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's April dept store sales up, supermkt down.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's April dept store sales up, supermkt down.

text.p: Mexico's department store sales rose 3.2 percent in April compared to the year-ago period, while supermarket sales fell 4.0 percent compared to April 1996, National Association of Self-Service and Department Stores (ANTAD) said Monday.
The association said in a statement that department store sales have been improving since January, with clothing sales for the month up 5.5 percent and appliance sales up 8.1 percent.

Sales are still far from recovering to pre-peso devaluation levels, ANTAD said. "In order to recover department store sale levels from 1994, growing at the current rates, the recovery will be will be reached at the end of 2003," it said.
In supermarket sales, ANTAD said the April decline is a seasonal phenomenon seen in recent years.
The four percent decline, "is regretably an aggravating factor to the ongoing internal consumption crisis, and a break with the positive trend that we thought had begun in March."
